Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, on the south bank of the Congo river at Pool Malebo. It was founded in 1881 by Henry Morton Stanley as a trading station called Léopoldville, and it is now one of the largest cities in Africa.

Stanley worked for King Leopold II of Belgium. The station lay just above the rapids that block the river from the sea, so it was where goods moved between river boats and the road, and later railway, to the coast. It grew under the Congo Free State and the Belgian Congo, and became the colony's capital in the 1920s. Across the river lies Brazzaville, capital of the other Congo.

At independence in 1960 Patrice Lumumba became prime minister here. In 1966 Mobutu renamed the city Kinshasa. It hosted the "Rumble in the Jungle" boxing match in 1974 and is the home of Congolese rumba, music heard across Africa. Its population has grown to well over ten million.
